notes: Every row's token spelling and purpose comes from the operator's own documentation, linked in `docs`, read on the date in `verified`.

`purpose` is the field most lists leave out and the one that changes the decision: `train` is a corpus for a future model, `answer` is a fetch made while a person waits for an answer that can cite and link you, `search` builds an index, `ads` checks ad landing pages, `preview` builds a link preview, and `agent` is a browser an assistant drives on one person’s behalf — a visitor, not a crawler.

`crawls: false` marks a control-only robots.txt token that fetches nothing by itself (Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended). Disallowing it changes how already-crawled content may be used; it does not remove you from search.
`respects_robots: false` marks an agent whose own operator documents that it may ignore robots.txt. For those, a robots.txt verdict states your request, not an outcome.

crawlers.note: A browser hosted by Anthropic and driven by an agent at one user’s direction, which Anthropic documents separately from its crawlers and fetchers. It carries the browser’s own User-Agent with the token added inside it, so a rule has to match the token rather than the whole string, and Anthropic publishes the addresses it comes from at claude.com/.well-known/sail under the same name. Anthropic states that a site’s preferences for its crawlers and for this traffic are independent of each other, and does not describe this traffic as governed by robots.txt.

A robots.txt token with no user-agent string of its own. It controls whether crawled content may train future Gemini models and ground answers in Gemini Apps and Vertex AI. Google documents that it does not affect inclusion in Google Search.
A generic crawler any Google product team may use, including one-off research crawls. Rules for it affect no named product.
Not an AI crawler, but AI Overviews are built from the Google index, so blocking it removes you from both.

Google documents that rules addressed to this token affect only crawls that a site owner has asked for when building a Vertex AI agent, and have no effect on Google Search or any other product. So it is the one row here that a site usually meets because somebody on that site asked for it.
Perplexity's own documentation states that because the fetch is user-initiated it generally ignores robots.txt.
Powers Spotlight, Siri and Safari search. Where robots.txt names Googlebot but not Applebot, Applebot follows the Googlebot rules.
Controls whether what Applebot already crawled may train Apple's foundation models. Apple documents that it crawls no pages and does not affect search results.
Crawls for Meta AI search results, which cite and link the content.
Meta documents that it may bypass robots.txt because it fetches single links at a user's request.
Builds the title, description and thumbnail for a shared link. Meta documents that it may bypass robots.txt for security and integrity checks.
Amazon documents that it may also be used to train Amazon AI models, honours allow/disallow, and may act on a robots.txt copy cached for up to 30 days.
Not an AI crawler, but Copilot answers are built on the Bing index.
Builds the public Common Crawl corpus, which many model builders then use. Blocking it after the fact does not remove you from archives already published.

Seen in logs and in other lists; no current operator page documenting the token was found on 2026-11-01.
